subject: Biotechnology
title: DNA Ligase: The Molecular Glue
description: A 60-second lesson on DNA Ligase: The Molecular Glue.

hook.text: Cutting DNA is useless without glue — DNA ligase seals the backbone, joining fragments permanently.

buildup.text: Ligase catalyzes a phosphodiester bond between adjacent nucleotides — stitching the sugar-phosphate backbone.

discovery.text: T4 DNA ligase from a virus is the workhorse — it joins both sticky and blunt ends of DNA fragments.

twist.text: Blunt-end ligation is inefficient — sticky ends are preferred because complementary overhangs guide alignment.

climax.text: Without ligase, recombinant DNA would be impossible — cut and paste needs both scissors and glue.

punchline.text: No glue, no genetic engineering — ligase makes it real.

quiz.question: Why is sticky-end ligation more efficient than blunt-end ligation?
options: Sticky ends use a different enzyme than blunt ends
Complementary single-stranded overhangs guide correct alignment before sealing
Blunt ends are always damaged during the cutting process
